stem: Near the end of the Guru Granth Sahib, the name Waheguru rings out again and again in Swayye (praise verses) by whom?
options: the Bhatts, bards of the Gurus' court
Bhagat Kabir, the weaver of Banaras
Sheikh Farid, the Sufi of Pakpattan
Balwand and Satta, the court musicians
why: The Swayye of the Bhatts, court bards who sang the Gurus' praises, close the main body of the Granth; in Bhatt Gayand's verses for Guru Ram Das, 'Waheguru' is repeated again and again. Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1402-1404.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Swayye of the Bhatts (Bhatt Gayand), Ang 1402-1404

es.stem: Cerca del final del Guru Granth Sahib, el nombre Waheguru resuena una y otra vez en los Swayye (versos de alabanza) de ¿quién?
options: los Bhatts, bardos de la corte de los Gurús
Bhagat Kabir, el tejedor de Benarés
Sheikh Farid, el sufí de Pakpattan
Balwand y Satta, los músicos de la corte
es.why: Los Swayye de los Bhatts, bardos de la corte que cantaban las alabanzas de los Gurús, cierran el cuerpo principal del Granth; en los versos de Bhatt Gayand para Guru Ram Das, 'Waheguru' se repite una y otra vez. Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1402-1404.

stem: Sikh tradition credits which Guru with shaping the Gurmukhi script, in which the Guru Granth Sahib is written?
options: Guru Arjan, the Fifth Guru
Guru Angad, the Second Guru
Guru Ram Das, the Fourth Guru
Guru Amar Das, the Third Guru
why: Sikh tradition remembers Guru Angad as the one who shaped and spread the Gurmukhi script, so ordinary people could read the Gurus' hymns for themselves; the whole Granth is written in it.
source: Sikh tradition on Guru Angad; Guru Granth Sahib (Gurmukhi script)

es.stem: La tradición sij atribuye a ¿qué Gurú haber dado forma a la escritura gurmukhi, en la que está escrito el Guru Granth Sahib?
options: Guru Arjan, el quinto Gurú
Guru Angad, el segundo Gurú
Guru Ram Das, el cuarto Gurú
Guru Amar Das, el tercer Gurú
es.why: La tradición sij recuerda a Guru Angad como quien dio forma a la escritura gurmukhi y la difundió, para que la gente común pudiera leer por sí misma los himnos de los Gurús; todo el Granth está escrito en ella.

stem: In Sikh teaching, as in Guru Arjan's Sukhmani Sahib, what do the paired words nirgun and sargun say about the One?
options: the soul is bound before and freed after the Name
the Guru's teaching is partly hidden, partly open
the One is past all qualities and in every form
two gods rule together, one far and one near
why: Nirgun is the One without qualities, beyond description; sargun is the same One present in every form. Sukhmani Sahib says the One is both at once, not two beings. Guru Granth Sahib, Gauri Sukhmani (Guru Arjan), Ang 287.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Gauri Sukhmani (Guru Arjan), Ang 287

es.stem: En la enseñanza sij, como en el Sukhmani Sahib de Guru Arjan, ¿qué dicen sobre el Uno las palabras pareadas nirgun y sargun?
options: el alma está atada antes del Nombre y libre después
la enseñanza del Gurú es en parte oculta y en parte abierta
el Uno está más allá de toda cualidad y en toda forma
dos dioses reinan juntos, uno lejano y otro cercano
es.why: Nirgun es el Uno sin cualidades, más allá de toda descripción; sargun es el mismo Uno presente en toda forma. El Sukhmani Sahib dice que el Uno es ambas cosas a la vez, no dos seres. Guru Granth Sahib, Gauri Sukhmani (Guru Arjan), Ang 287.

stem: In Raag Nat, Guru Ram Das sings 'bani guru, guru hai bani'. What does that line say about the Guru?
options: the hymns count only when a living Guru sings them
the hymns are a lesser copy of a Guru in a body
the hymns must be read aloud by a Guru's own family
the Word sung in the hymns is itself the Guru
why: Guru Ram Das says the bani (the Word in the Gurus' hymns) is the Guru and the Guru is the bani, with all nectar within it; this is why Sikhs bow to the Granth as the Word, not as paper. Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Nat, Ang 982.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Nat (Guru Ram Das), Ang 982

es.stem: En el Raag Nat, Guru Ram Das canta 'bani guru, guru hai bani'. ¿Qué dice ese verso sobre el Gurú?
options: los himnos solo cuentan si los canta un Gurú vivo
los himnos son una copia menor de un Gurú en un cuerpo
los himnos debe leerlos en voz alta la familia del Gurú
la Palabra cantada en los himnos es en sí el Gurú
es.why: Guru Ram Das dice que la bani (la Palabra en los himnos de los Gurús) es el Gurú y el Gurú es la bani, con todo néctar dentro de ella; por eso los sijs se inclinan ante el Granth como Palabra, no como papel. Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Nat, Ang 982.

stem: In a salok of Asa di Var, Guru Nanak gives each of the four ages (yugas) a chariot and a charioteer. What do the chariots and drivers stand for?
options: the kings who ruled the land in each age
the virtues or vices that move people
the length of a human life in each age
the holy places people visited in each age
why: Guru Nanak names a chariot and driver for each age: contentment and righteousness in Satjug, down to the fire of craving and falsehood in Kaljug. The ages are told by what moves people's hearts. Guru Granth Sahib, Asa di Var, Ang 470.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Asa di Var, salok of Guru Nanak, Ang 470

es.stem: En un salok del Asa di Var, Guru Nanak da a cada una de las cuatro edades (yugas) un carro y un auriga. ¿Qué representan los carros y sus aurigas?
options: los reyes que gobernaron la tierra en cada edad
las virtudes o los vicios que mueven a la gente
la duración de la vida humana en cada edad
los lugares santos que se visitaban en cada edad
es.why: Guru Nanak nombra un carro y un auriga para cada edad: el contento y la rectitud en el Satjug, hasta el fuego del deseo y la falsedad en el Kaljug. Las edades se describen por lo que mueve el corazón de la gente. Guru Granth Sahib, Asa di Var, Ang 470.

stem: A Sikh village is in a bitter land dispute with a neighbouring chief, and no talks have been tried yet. Which course fits the Tenth Guru's teaching in his Zafarnama?
options: take up arms now, since the cause is just
refuse all force, even if every talk fails
try every peaceful means first, arms last
let the emperor's court settle it for them
why: In the Zafarnama, his letter to Aurangzeb, Guru Gobind Singh writes that when all other means have failed, it is right to take up the sword. A just cause alone is not enough, force is not ruled out for good, and untried talks come first. Dasam Granth, Zafarnama.
source: Zafarnama of Guru Gobind Singh (Dasam Granth)

es.stem: Una aldea sij tiene una dura disputa de tierras con un jefe vecino, y aún no se ha intentado dialogar. ¿Qué camino concuerda con la enseñanza del décimo Gurú en su Zafarnama?
options: tomar las armas ya, porque la causa es justa
rechazar toda fuerza, aunque falle todo diálogo
intentar antes toda vía pacífica; armas al final
dejar que el tribunal del emperador lo resuelva
es.why: En el Zafarnama, su carta a Aurangzeb, Guru Gobind Singh escribe que, cuando todos los demás medios han fallado, es justo tomar la espada. Una causa justa no basta por sí sola, la fuerza no queda descartada para siempre y el diálogo no intentado va primero. Dasam Granth, Zafarnama.

stem: What do Sikhs mean by 'Guru Granth, Guru Panth', and what did Guru Gobind Singh do that the phrase remembers?
why: Guru Gobind Singh named no human successor; before his death at Nanded in 1708 he passed the guruship to the scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, and to the Khalsa Panth, the community, which makes serious decisions in the Granth's presence.
source: Sikh tradition on the succession of 1708 (Nanded); Sikh Rehat Maryada

rubric.point: Says the guruship rests in the scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib. Saying only that Sikhs respect the book, without calling it the Guru, counts as partly.
Says the community (the Panth or Khalsa) also carries the Guru's authority, together with the Granth. Mentioning only the book counts as partly.
Mentions that Guru Gobind Singh named no human successor (Nanded, 1708), or that the community decides serious matters (gurmata) in the Granth's presence (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: ¿Qué quieren decir los sijs con 'Guru Granth, Guru Panth', y qué hizo Guru Gobind Singh que esa frase recuerda?
es.why: Guru Gobind Singh no nombró un sucesor humano; antes de morir en Nanded en 1708, pasó la condición de Gurú a la escritura, el Guru Granth Sahib, y al Khalsa Panth, la comunidad, que toma las decisiones importantes en presencia del Granth.

stem: In the Sikh langar, why is the meal eaten in pangat, seated in rows on the floor, and what does this teach?
why: The langar is a free kitchen open to all; eating in pangat, in one row at one height from one pot, sets aside caste, rank and creed and makes the teaching that one Light is in everyone visible. Tradition says even the emperor Akbar sat in the row before meeting Guru Amar Das.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ramkali ki Var of Balwand and Satta, Ang 967; Sikh tradition on Guru Amar Das

rubric.point: Says everyone sits together at the same level, so no one is placed above another by caste, wealth, rank or religion. 'It is tidy' or 'it is tradition' alone does not count.
Links it to equality: the meal shows that all people are equal, or that the same divine Light is in everyone. Naming equality without the seating counts as partly.
Mentions that the langar is free and open to anyone, or the story of Akbar sitting in pangat before meeting Guru Amar Das, or Mata Khivi's langar (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el langar sij, ¿por qué se come en pangat, sentados en filas en el suelo, y qué enseña esto?
es.why: El langar es una cocina gratuita abierta a todos; comer en pangat, en una sola fila, a la misma altura y de la misma olla, deja de lado la casta, el rango y el credo, y hace visible la enseñanza de que la misma Luz está en todos. La tradición dice que hasta el emperador Akbar se sentó en la fila antes de reunirse con Guru Amar Das.
